S1.why: Adverb مجاناً avoids making an adjective agree with the invariant loan كاتلينج; the tiles above already say what is counted.

S2.why: Plain imperative invitation, 11 letters; carries 'beyond the free ones' through المزيد without any limit or sales word.

S3.s: حفظت %lld كاتلينج، وهو كل ما تتسع له النسخة المجانية. ستبقى لك مجاناً وتعمل كما هي.
S3.back: you-saved 5 Cutling, and-it all what holds for-it the-version the-free. they-will-remain for-you free and-work as they-are.
S3.why: Names the cap through النسخة المجانية (same phrase as S28) and reassures with ستبقى لك; كاتلينج after the number as the vocab writes counts.

S4.why: Imperative states the allowance without the 'you can' frame; number then invariant كاتلينج, as in the vocab's count string.

S5.why: Same verb حفظ as S3 and S4; numbers stay in source order, so plain %lld needs no positional form.

S6.why: Bold line as a noun phrase; مساحة is the word used for room throughout (S22).

S7.s: احفظ حتى %@ كاتلينج نصي و%lld صورة.
S7.back: save up-to 5,000 Cutling textual and-500 image.
S7.why: كاتلينج نصي is the vocab's own name for a text item; صورة stays singular, which is correct Arabic after hundreds and thousands.

S8.why: Arabic lists repeat و before each item and attach it to the Latin name, as Apple's Arabic pages write it.

S9.s: شراء واحد يشملها كلها بحساب Apple الخاص بك.
S9.back: purchase one covers-them all-of-them with-account Apple the-belonging to-you.
S9.why: حساب Apple الخاص بك is the vocab's exact phrase; يشملها كلها points back at the three devices in the bold line.

S10.why: Second person present tense, warmer than the noun دفعة واحدة, and says nothing recurs.

S11.s: بلا اشتراك ولا إعلانات ولا إنشاء حساب.
S11.back: without subscription and-no advertisements and-no creating account.
S11.why: بلا … ولا … ولا is the native chain for three absences; إنشاء حساب keeps sign-up apart from the vocab's تسجيل الدخول (sign-in).

S12.why: The wording Arabic iOS apps use for the App Store restore action; verbal noun like the app's other buttons (متابعة).

S13.why: جارٍ + verbal noun is the iOS Arabic in-progress form; ends with the ellipsis character.

S14.why: النسخة الكاملة is how Arabic apps name the unlocked app and avoids the clash between Cutling the app and كاتلينج the item; verbal noun as on the app's buttons; 21 letters plus the price.

S15.why: S14 without the price, so the button does not change words when the price loads.

S16.why: The iOS Arabic 'Not Now': putting it off, not refusing.

S17.why: The iOS Arabic label for close buttons, verbal noun.

S18.why: Warm and short (13 letters); كله with the app as masculine, so it reads as the whole app and all its room.

S19.s: شكراً لك. شراؤك يدعم كاتلينج ومن يطوّره وحده.
S19.back: thanks to-you. your-purchase supports Cutling and-who develops-it alone.
S19.why: من يطوّره وحده says 'the one person who makes it' the way a speaker would, without the stiff الشخص الوحيد الذي.

S20.s: أهلاً بعودتك. عادت إليك النسخة الكاملة.
S20.back: welcome with-your-return. returned to-you the-version the-full.
S20.why: أهلاً بعودتك is the everyday Arabic greeting for a returning person; the verb عاد echoes it.

S21.why: Spoken version of S5; من أصل makes 'out of' unmistakable by ear.

S22.why: The invariant loan كاتلينج after the number reads correctly for 1, 2, 5 and 21, so no Arabic plural forms are needed, as in the vocab's count string.
